jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Billionaire Bouquet
jokes.joke: I went to a flower shop and said, “I need something that says I’m sorry.” The florist said, “Normal sorry or billionaire sorry?” I said, “What’s billionaire sorry?” She said, “You buy one rose, underpay everyone, then name the whole garden after yourself.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Dream Home
jokes.joke: My real estate agent told me the neighborhood was 'up and coming.' That was six years ago. I'm still waiting. Last week I asked her what's happening with the area and she said, 'Oh, it's exploding.' I looked it up. A gas main broke. She wasn't wrong — I just keep choosing to hear what I want to hear, which I think is her actual sales strategy.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Roadside Assistance
seedTermsUsed: Having to decide to help or do not
jokes.joke: I drove past a real estate agent struggling to change a flat tire in the pouring rain. I was torn on whether to help or not. Do I pull over and lend a hand? Or do I just roll down my window, call the puddle a “breathtaking waterfront feature,” and step on the gas?

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Billionaire Discipline
jokes.joke: Folks, I'm pretty gullible. I bought into the whole billionaire routine - be disciplined, wake at dawn, hustle nonstop. Tried it for a month straight. My big win? Realizing how much I missed sleeping in. Those billionaires are probably laughing from their yachts, raking in cash from the self-help books they sold suckers like me. Now my only discipline is hitting snooze on that nonsense.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Bloom & Doom
jokes.joke: I tried to impress someone by buying fancy flowers, but the florist saw how gullible I am. She said, “These blooms are perfect for attracting love.” I got home, set them out, and realized she meant they attract bees. Nothing kills the mood faster than me sprinting around my apartment yelling, “I bought romance, not a swarm!”

scores.comment: Clear premise and believable real-estate spin; the gas-main turn is solid, but the final line explains the joke more than it heightens it.
Clean first-person setup, strong real-estate reframing, and the waterfront-feature punchline lands crisply.
Competent but familiar billionaire self-help skepticism; it also uses disciplined as a third seed concept, so prompt fit is capped.
Readable and concrete, with a decent bees/romance reversal, but the wording feels sitcom-broad and the payoff is only mildly funny.

Clean three-beat structure with a genuinely good punchline. The billionaires sorry framing is specific and earned, not vague. The final line lands with rhythm and a real comic image. Tight, stageable, no wasted words.

The pivot from sympathy to waterfront feature is the best surprise in the batch—unexpected, character-specific, and funny without explanation. Natural first-person voice throughout. The closing gas-pedal beat earns it.

The premise is familiar (billionaire hustle culture skepticism) and the turn is predictable. Hitting snooze on that nonsense is a weak closer. Uses three seed terms as concepts (gullible, billionaires, disciplined), so promptFit is penalized. Competent but forgettable.

The bee-swap is a clean misdirect and the closer has energy, but I bought romance, not a swarm slightly over-explains what just happened. Solid and stageable, just not sharp enough to hit 7. Prompt fit is excellent—exactly two concepts used naturally.
Strong rhythm and classic rule of three in the punchline. Very economical setup and delivery.
Solid misdirection with the gas main turn, but the final sentence slightly over-explains the premise.
Prompt fit penalized for using three seed terms (gullible, billionaires, disciplined). Lacks a sharp turn; reads more like a generic rant than stand-up.
Amusing imagery and competent structure, though the final shouted dialogue feels a bit cartoonish rather than natural spoken stand-up.
Clever dialogue but mild payoff, more wordplay than strong laugh.
Solid twist on realtor speak with self-aware gullibility; good timing.
Amusing premise twist but feels slightly forced in execution.
Clear visual punch but predictable misdirection on attracting love.
Clean premise and a solid billionaire turn; mild but real payoff.
Relatable angle with a tidy turn; steady, not standout.
Good escalation and a clear snap; humorous image lands.
Coherent but leans conversational; punchline softens.
